title: Travel tin soy candle
subtitle: A small lidded soy wax candle for travel
excerpt: A small soy wax candle poured into a lidded metal tin: 100 to 120 g of wax, single wick, fragranced at 7% of wax weight. The tin makes the candle portable and the lid snuffs the flame cleanly without soot. Makes four 30 ml tins from 100 g of soy wax; cure five to seven days before burning.
sourceNotes: Container candle technique in Candlemaking by Betty Oppenheimer (1999). Metal tin pour temperature notes: tins conduct heat better than glass and cool the wax surface faster, sometimes producing a depression at the centre; a light re-pour fills this. Pour temperature for soy container wax in metal tins: 60 to 65°C.

recipe.yieldDescription: 4 × 30 ml travel tins (~25 g wax each)
recipe.batchNotes: Pour as many tins as needed from a larger melt. Keep tins on a level surface until fully set, tins sit unevenly on some worktops.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cure five to seven days before the first burn. Travel candles make good gifts; make a batch at least a week before gifting.
recipe.temperatureNote: Pour at 60 to 65°C. Metal tins cool the wax quickly; pour at the higher end of this range to get a clean, flat surface.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Two years in a cool, dry place. The lid seals the scent well when the candle is stored; keep it on when not burning.

glossaryTerms.definition: The first burn of a container candle, which sets the melt pool. In a small tin, the first burn may melt fully to the tin edge in one to two hours.
The resting period after pouring. Five to seven days for soy wax gives the fragrance time to bind with the wax, improving scent throw.

content.text: A travel tin candle is a small soy wax candle poured into a lidded metal tin, fragranced at 7% of wax weight with your choice of scent. The tin is portable and the lid snuffs the flame cleanly without soot when the candle is finished for the evening. Makes four 30 ml tins from 100 g of soy wax;
five to seven days before burning.

items.prepNote: 7% of wax weight; substitute any fragrance or essential oil with a flash point above 70°C
pre-tabbed cotton wick for a 40 to 50 mm diameter tin (CD-6 or ECO-4 size)

content.text: Press a wick tab to the base of each tin and hold in place with a centring bar across the rim. Set the four tins on a flat, level surface.

Melt the soy wax to 75°C, cool to 65°C, stir in the fragrance or essential oil for 30 seconds, and pour into the four tins in one pass. Metal tins cool the wax surface faster than glass and may produce a slight depression at the centre as the wax contracts. If this happens, pour a small top-up of wax at 65°C once the first pour has set.
Trim the wicks to 6 mm after 24 hours and put the lids on. Cure for five to seven days before the first burn.

: burn for one to two hours on the first light until the melt pool reaches the tin edge. To extinguish, press the lid on, it snuffs the flame instantly. Trim the wick to 6 mm before every subsequent burn.
Two years in a cool, dry place. The sealed tin protects the scent well; a travel candle stored with the lid on holds its scent longer than an open jar candle.
